title: Feathers in the wind
hook: a folk tale: gossip is like feathers from a pillow, impossible to gather back

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was motzi shem ra, bringing out a bad name, and your line: no false names. Today, a tale about how far words go once they leave.

A pillow, a knife, and a windy hill. That's the whole set for a story Jewish teachers tell about speech. Someone in a small town has been spreading talk about a neighbor. The talk turns out to be cruel, and the person, sick about it, goes to the rabbi to ask how to make it right. The rabbi says: take a feather pillow up the hill, cut it open, and come back. Strange, but easy. The person slits the pillow, watches the wind take the feathers, and comes back, ready to be forgiven. Good, says the rabbi. Now go and gather every feather.
screen: `A PILLOW, A KNIFE, A WINDY HILL.` → `CUT IT OPEN.` → `NOW GATHER EVERY FEATHER.`

segments.voice: Feathers in the wind. Turn the tale four ways. First, where it comes from. You won't find it in the Torah or the Talmud. It's a folk tale, and tellers hang it on different rabbis and different towns. It doesn't need a famous source to land: anyone who has opened a pillow knows how feathers behave. Second, the shape of the lesson. Scattering takes a moment. Gathering takes forever, and still fails. Words leave in a breath, land in ears you'll never meet, and get repeated in voices that aren't yours. Third, who the story is about. Not a villain. Someone who is sorry and wants to fix it. The tale doesn't say repentance is useless; yesterday's repair still matters. But even real regret can't recall every feather. Some of the harm is already past reaching. Fourth, so the care belongs before the words. Proverbs puts the stakes bluntly: "Death and life are in the power of the tongue." The tale turns that line into something you can see. And today a pillow opens with one tap. A forwarded message, a screenshot, a post: each a feather with a timestamp, blowing over hills the sender will never climb. The moment of most control is the second before speaking, while every feather is still inside.
screen: `A FOLK TALE, NOT A TALMUD PAGE.` · `EASY TO SCATTER, HARD TO GATHER.` · `EVEN REAL REGRET CAN'T RECALL THEM.` · `DEATH AND LIFE IN THE TONGUE.` · then, large: `YOU CAN'T GATHER FEATHERS.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a conversation coming up, a call, a meeting, a group chat, and one sentence already waiting on your tongue: a joke at someone's expense, a complaint about someone absent, news that isn't yours to share. Hold it like a pillow in your hands and ask where it could blow once it's out. Decide now, while it's still sealed, whether it goes out at all; if you pray, you can ask for a guarded mouth.
Feathers in the wind. A folk tale: harmful words, like a pillow's feathers, scatter in a moment and can never all be gathered back. Today's word.
Your line: you can't gather feathers. Every one is still inside until you speak. See you on the hill.

howItsDone: Jewish teachers, parents and schools often tell the feathers tale when teaching about lashon hara, as a picture of why harmful speech can't be fully undone.
